subject: Physics
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate, never a learner estimate; teaching depth is intrinsic while practice support is routed separately.

rungs.aha: A vector is not fixed by size alone: direction is part of the quantity, and a unit vector can carry direction independently of magnitude.
learner_owns: Can compare ordinary scalar sizes and recognise an arrow as having an orientation.
must_contain: Two equal-length arrows pointing in different directions.
A direction-only arrow normalised to the same unit length from different starting magnitudes.

misconception.wrong_idea: Two directed quantities with the same magnitude are the same vector.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: Two arrows are both 5 units long, one east and one north. Are they the same directed quantity?
misconception.repair: State both size and direction; changing either changes the vector. Normalising removes size while preserving direction.

rungs.closure: Given two arrows with equal size, distinguish whether they represent the same vector and identify the directional information that decides.

controlled_variation.notice: equal magnitude does not make two directed quantities equal

controlled_variation.vary: the original arrow length before normalising
controlled_variation.notice: the unit-direction arrow is unchanged by the original magnitude

rungs.aha: Vector addition combines directed quantities geometrically or component by component; input magnitudes cannot simply be added unless the directions make that valid.
learner_owns: A vector is not fixed by size alone: direction is part of the quantity, and a unit vector can carry direction independently of magnitude.
must_contain: A tail-to-head construction and the same addition resolved along declared axes.
Two equal input magnitudes at different included angles.

misconception.wrong_idea: The magnitude of A + B is always |A| + |B|.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: Two 5-unit vectors point in opposite directions. Is the magnitude of their sum 10?
misconception.repair: Preserve direction while combining; use geometry or signed components, and treat direct magnitude addition as a special collinear case rather than a general rule.

rungs.closure: For two vectors at a stated angle, construct or compute their sum and explain why the result's magnitude is or is not the sum of the input magnitudes.

controlled_variation.vary: the angle between two fixed-length vectors
controlled_variation.notice: the resultant length changes from large to small even though the inputs do not

controlled_variation.vary: the order in which the two vectors are placed tail-to-head
controlled_variation.notice: the final resultant is unchanged, exposing commutativity of addition

must_contain: A second arrow reversed without rescaling before addition.
The same pair evaluated in both subtraction orders.

controlled_variation.vary: which operand is subtracted from which
controlled_variation.notice: the difference arrow reverses while its magnitude stays the same

rungs.aha: A cross product produces an axial direction perpendicular to the input plane; reversing operand order keeps its magnitude but flips that out-of-plane direction.
learner_owns: Vector subtraction is addition of the reversed second vector, so operand order matters even though ordinary vector addition is commutative.
must_contain: A clearly drawn plane containing both polar input vectors and a separate out-of-plane axial result.
Both operand orders displayed for the same input pair.

misconception.wrong_idea: A cross product is commutative, so swapping A and B leaves the out-of-plane result unchanged.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: For perpendicular A and B, compare A × B with B × A. Do their out-of-plane arrows point the same way?
misconception.repair: Keep the input plane fixed, use the ordered pair to choose the perpendicular axial direction, and reverse that direction when the operand order reverses.

rungs.closure: Given two nonparallel vectors and an oriented plane, state the cross-product direction for both operand orders and identify the sign reversal.

controlled_variation.hold: the same two input vectors and the same oriented plane
controlled_variation.notice: the axial arrow flips from one side of the plane to the other while its magnitude stays unchanged

controlled_variation.vary: the angle between the vectors from perpendicular toward parallel
controlled_variation.notice: the axial arrow shortens to zero as the input directions become parallel

family.invariant_demand: Identify the requested vector operation, preserve magnitude and directional information, carry operand order where it matters, and verify the result against a geometrically equivalent construction.
family.difficult_move: Deciding which directional operation the wording encodes and preserving its orientation while translating between components, in-plane arrows, and an out-of-plane axial result.
family.independent_check: Use an alternate representation: component and arrow results must agree; reversing subtraction operands negates the result, and reversing cross-product operands flips the axial direction.

support_ladder.handed_over: The requested operation, axis directions, and a partially constructed diagram are supplied.
The requested operation and axis directions are supplied.
Only the physical or geometric description and requested quantity are supplied.

transfer.changed_demand: A new situation presents two directed quantities and the learner must decide whether the task requires addition, subtraction, or an out-of-plane cross product.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which operation the physical wording encodes

transfer.changed_demand: Two vectors are given only by a scaled arrow diagram and the result must be expressed in signed components.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the component values of the input arrows

transfer.changed_demand: The cross-product inputs lie in an unfamiliar tilted plane rather than the page plane, so the axial result must still be oriented perpendicular to that plane.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which side of the tilted plane corresponds to the ordered axial direction
